newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM Rauma dividend signals focus - CEO.
newsitem.headline: UPM Rauma dividend signals focus - CEO.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene Oy's decision to pay part of its 1996 dividend in shares in its 73-percent owned Rauma Oy signals an increased focus on forestry, UPM's CEO said on Tuesday.

"This is a clear signal that UPM-Kymmene is striving to focus exclusively on the forestry industry and that Rauma will become independent," CEO Juha Niemela told a news conference after UPM reported 1996 profits down 43 percent on 1995.
UPM-Kymmene earlier said in a statement with its 1996 results that it would pay 3.00 markka of its proposed 4.50 markka 1996 dividend in Rauma shares.
The share dividend would reduce UPM's stake in Rauma to 59.9 percent, and the company said it intended to cut its stake further, below 50 percent.
No decision has been made on when UPM would push its stake below 50 percent, Niemela said, and added that the share dividend would be "unique" as a means of lowering UPM's Rauma shareholding.
"By this (move) we also want to broaden Rauma's ownership base. This is also very important," Niemela said.
Since it obtained a Wall Street listing in mid-1995, trade in Rauma's ADRs has been thinner than UPM had expected, he said.
"Rauma's liquidity (in New York) has been too low," said UPM-Kymmene chief financial officer Jan-Henrik Kulp.
Asked what strategic importance UPM-Kymmene placed on its 3.9 percent stake (over 10 percent of the votes) in Finnish telecoms group Nokia Oy, Niemela said it was a "strategic security factor."
"It has no strategic business value," he said, adding that it would also have been possible to distribute Nokia shares as dividend.
